heroSubtitle: SWIRL is a pooled mixing layer for Lightning payments: a continuously deepening anonymity pool, uniform denominations, blinded paths in both directions — and a submarine-swap exit that leaves the chain with nothing to cluster.

logoBar.label: BOLT12 · BLINDED PATHS · DEEP POOL · SUBMARINE SWAPS

useCases.title: THE PROTOCOL
useCases.subtitle: Three layers. Zero linkage.
useCases.intro: Privacy is a property of systems, not primitives. SWIRL stacks three independent layers — identity, flow, settlement — each engineered to close a different oracle.
useCases.showcaseCaption: From scan to settlement, no observer — on-chain or off-chain — can reconstruct the flow.
useCases.onlineDesc: A static BOLT12 code that never names your node. Payers negotiate one-time invoices over onion-routed messages, and every reply ends in a blinded path whose final hops are ECDH-derived pseudonyms.
useCases.inPersonDesc: Deposits enter a pool that never closes, over unannounced channels. Exits are cut into uniform denominations, shuffled against every live deposit, and released through a randomized delay queue — amount, order and timing all carry zero bits.
useCases.agentsDesc: When funds touch layer 1, they cross a hashlock-atomic submarine swap into a fresh UTXO with no shared history. In ≠ out — on the graph and on the chain.
useCases.checkoutNote: Below is what a payer sees when they scan your code.

privacy.title: WHAT STAYS HIDDEN
privacy.subtitle: Lightning is fast. It was never private.
privacy.intro: Every payment that crosses the public graph leaves a metadata trail: node identities, channel positions, timing signatures. SWIRL is engineered so that this trail never forms in the first place.

feature1Desc: One static BOLT12 offer issues a fresh invoice to every payer. Your node ID and channel topology never appear on it — the final hops are blinded, single-use pseudonyms.
feature2Desc: Deposits deepen one shared pool that never closes. Payouts leave in uniform denominations, shuffled and time-jittered, so amount and ordering stop identifying anyone.
feature3Desc: An atomic submarine swap moves funds into a fresh UTXO with no shared history. Your on-chain footprint begins exactly where your past ends.
howItWorksTitle: From payer to ghost in three moves
step1Desc: Post one static code. It mints one-time invoices indefinitely.
step2Desc: Payments dissolve into one deep, shuffled pool.
step3Desc: Exit atomically to a UTXO with no past.
roadSub: Four routes. Each one strips a power from the coordinator.
road1v: SNARK exits. The pool sees a proof, never a link.
road2v: Timelocked refunds, multisig legs. Worst case is refusal — never theft.
road3v: PTLCs re-blind every hop. The public graph loses the thread.
road4v: BitVM3 fraud proofs settle the large lanes. No operator needed.
integrationsSubtitle: Every component earns its place in the threat model
intHostedDesc: Static codes that negotiate per-payment invoices over onion messages. No server in the loop, no identifier ever reused.
intApiDesc: Payers route to pseudonyms, not to you. Relays and the public graph learn nothing about the final destination.
intWidgetDesc: Pool ingress rides channels that never enter public gossip — no funding outpoint connects the pool to layer 1.
intShopifyDesc: Every exit is cut from the same set of standard amounts. Value itself stops being a fingerprint.
intWooDesc: No accounts, no identity, no keys surrendered. Your claim on the exit is a sealed receipt credential only you hold — not a login, not an email.
intMcpDesc: Pool state lives in memory and dies with the process. There is no database to leak, and none to subpoena.
agentsSubtitle: What chain analysis already knows about Lightning
agentsDesc: Invoice resolution reveals the receiver's node. Gossip reveals its channels. Channel closes reveal its UTXOs. Chaining exactly these public signals, researchers have already linked 46% of the network's nodes back to on-chain entities.
agentsDescHighlight: SWIRL breaks that chain at every link.
agentsStep2: A one-time invoice is negotiated privately
agentsStep4: It dissolves into the deep pool
